access: Recommended lesson completed in the signed-in Chrome session on the free tier.
knowledge_learned: For a fixed positive modulus, replace each operand by its remainder before adding or multiplying. Reduce the result again to get a remainder in the correct range.
Parity is arithmetic modulo 2. Twice an odd number leaves remainder 2 modulo 4, and every odd square leaves remainder 1 modulo 8.
A repeating cycle of six colours labels residues modulo 6. Two labels suffice to predict the product’s label, even when the original numbers are hidden.
mechanics_observed: Worked place-value and last-digit examples lead into prediction questions about sums and products.
Some answer choices are unreduced sums or products, testing whether the learner applies the modulus again.
Practice transfers from explicit remainders to parity, large squares and a hidden-product prediction using a repeating colour cycle.
Each prediction uses an explicit Check action, immediate feedback and an optional Why explanation. Progress ends with a Finish action.
